The gaps are hardening and edge cases beyond the request, listed above.

The merged patch adds extra safety: it cancels in-flight batch jobs, uses a safer ordering, and adds a backend race guard. Those go beyond the request.

results.evidence: moveToDraft calls hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., {status:'draft'}) and saveBroadcastFinished(draft), making isReadOnly false. But the scheduled send is not removed or paused here; whether the backend scheduler skips draft flows depends on backend code (not shown). Frontend-only patch; c8 suggests scheduler doesn't re-verify status.

`canMoveToDraft = !!broadcast && !batchJobsLoading && getBroadcastStatus(broadcast, {latestBatchJob, totals:{}}) === 'scheduled'` — only shown for a scheduled status (live with pending schedule); draft or already-sent not 'scheduled' (assuming getBroadcastStatus semantics).

launchBroadcast lists existing schedules and destroys all via hogFlowsSchedulesDestroy before activating, then creates one new schedule via hogFlowsSchedulesCreate for later/recurring; for 'now' none is created, so no leftover.

Schedules are listed and destroyed before `activated = await hogFlowsPartialUpdate(..., {status:'active'})`; the broadcast is saved as draft (buildBroadcastPayload status 'draft') until then. Interruption during replacement leaves draft.
canMoveToDraft only checks batchJobsLoading and status==='scheduled'; no check for more than one schedule or for a workflow shape the wizard can't edit.
Button onClick={() => moveToDraft()} directly; no confirmation dialog.
moveToDraft only patches status to draft and shows 'Broadcast moved to draft'; no cancellation of started runs or differentiated messages.
No scheduler/backend changes in the patch; no status re-verification before run creation.
Existing schedules are destroyed and the new schedule is built with only rrule, starts_at, timezone; variables from the old schedule are not carried over.

result:
I added a "Move to draft" button for live scheduled broadcasts and made launching replace any existing schedule. I didn't run tests, typecheck or lint, and I didn't add a test. Everything is frontend, in `products/workflows/frontend/Broadcasts/`.

- **Move to draft:** `BroadcastSummary.tsx` shows a "Move to draft" button, only when the broadcast is still waiting on its schedule (status `scheduled`, no run started). It sets the flow back to `draft` and reopens the wizard on the review step. The new `moveToDraft` action in `broadcastWizardLogic.ts` also adds a `movingToDraft` loading flag, so the button can't be double-clicked.
- **Relaunch bug:** `launchBroadcast` now lists the broadcast's existing schedules and deletes them before it activates the flow. The fresh schedule it creates is always active. This covers the case where editing a draft's audience paused the old schedule, and it also means a leftover schedule can't linger on an immediate send. The schedule status is still not writable through the API; replacing the schedule works around that instead of changing it.

The old schedule is deleted before activation, so an activation or create failure leaves the broadcast as a draft with no schedule. The existing catch already reverts to draft in that case, and the user can launch again.

I only added the button on the summary page. The Broadcasts list is unchanged.
